text:
The checkout-button test claimed a 4.1% conversion lift, but the assignment logs disagree. The split was meant to be 50/50, yet 51.8% of the 212,000 users went to treatment. A chi-square check puts the p-value for this sample ratio mismatch below 0.001, so the randomization was broken. The bot filter was deployed on day 6 to only the treatment variant's edge servers, and it quietly removed low-intent sessions from one arm.

The team also checked the results every day and shipped as soon as the p-value dipped below 0.05 on day 9. Stopping the test at the first good-looking result, after daily looks, raises the false-positive rate from the nominal 5% to roughly 20-30%.

The lift is also probably a novelty effect. Day-1 cohorts converted at twice the rate of day-12 cohorts, so I suspect most of the lift came from that.

Before anyone puts this number on a roadmap, rerun the test with a fixed duration, alerts for sample ratio mismatch, and a pipeline that doesn't change mid-test. As it stands, the lift is a mirage, even though it comes with a confidence interval.
